method.method_draft: Decompose the hexagon geometrically. Draw/use the three extended side lines P-A-B-S, Q-A-C-T, and U-C-B-R, as indicated in the image. These partition PQRSTU into the central triangle ABC, three corner triangles APQ, BRS, CTU, and three trapezoids ABRQ, BCST, CAPU. Each corner triangle has area 1 because, for example, AP=AB and AQ=AC and the included angle has the same sine as angle BAC; similarly for BRS and CTU. For trapezoid ABRQ, the bases AB and QR are parallel, QR=2AB, and the distance between them equals the altitude from C to AB, so area(ABRQ)=((AB+2AB)/2)h=3 area(ABC)=3. The two analogous trapezoids BCST and CAPU also each have area 3. Therefore total area = central 1 + three corner triangles 3*1 + three trapezoids 3*3 = 13.
